name: Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd.
business_summary: Maharatna PSU (government 63%) manufacturing power-plant equipment (thermal BTG sets, boilers, turbines, generators), transmission (transformers, HVDC), industrial products, railway rolling stock/propulsion, renewable, oil and gas, and defence systems. FY26 sales Rs33,782 cr, TTM Rs37,782 cr (+29%), EBITDA margin 10% (from 4-5%), PAT Rs2,879 cr; Q2 FY27 sales Rs9,300 cr, EBITDA Rs1,026 cr, PAT Rs821 cr. Order book up 17% (T&D India 2026-10-15). Market cap Rs146,073 cr at 51x P/E, ROE 6%, borrowings down to Rs6,018 cr. Government stake 63% (promoter 58.17%).

exposures.mechanism: Thermal capacity addition programme (~80+ GW planned; model knowledge) is the dominant demand driver; +3pp demand growth raises ordering confidence. Adani Power awarded BHEL up to Rs28,000 cr for four projects totalling 6,400 MW (2026-11-04). +3pp => ~+8% BTG order flow; revenue lag 2-3 years; EBITDA op. leverage 2x on 10% margin; EV/MCap 1.0, persistence 0.6 => ~+3.

evidence.note: Business Standard/Financial Express: BHEL bags up to Rs28,000 cr Adani Power orders; shares +6%

exposures.mechanism: Private thermal developers (Adani, JSW, Tata Power) and industrial customers ordering power equipment; +10% private capex => ~+4% order inflow => +2.0.
NTPC/state gencos, nuclear, railways (transportation) and defence-adjacent orders are PSU/government funded; +10% capex => ~+5% order flow, x2 op. leverage x0.5 persistence => ~+3.0.
Transmission segment (transformers, HVDC/FACTS, switchgear) benefits from grid build-out; smaller share than power BTG.
Transportation segment (locomotives, EMU/Vande Bharat propulsion, Kavach); +10% => ~+1% equity.
Discom health and PSU gencos' ability to fund capex; receivable cycle of BHEL improves with reform progress.

Steel, castings and forgings ~14% of sales on long fixed-price contracts with only partial price-variation clauses. +7% => ~1.0% of sales vs 10% TTM EBITDA margin => -10% EBITDA; ~50% unrecovered => -5% x persistence 0.5 x EV/MCap 1.0 => -2.5, shaded to -2.0. Empirical F_STEEL_GLOBAL +1.92 (t=1.7) and F_IRON_ORE +5.73 (t=2.8) are positive and contradict the sign: they reflect the capital-goods/commodity-cycle beta (BHEL beta 1.7-1.8) rather than cost pass-through; the model should use the fundamental sign with a wide range.
Copper windings and cabling ~4% of sales; +10% => 0.4% of sales => -4% EBITDA, half recoverable => -2% x 0.5 x 1.0 => ~-0.6 (empirical +0.89 t=0.9 contradicts, cycle proxy).

Borrowings Rs6,018 cr (down from Rs9,015 cr) with interest Rs125 cr/quarter: +25bp = Rs15 cr = ~0.4% of EBITDA; main effect is the 50x P/E and customers' project financing. Repo 5.50% since 2026-10-07.

evidence.note: Google News: Reuters 2026-10-07 'India first hike in nearly 4 years'; SCC Online 'repo to 5.50%, calibrated tightening'

exposures.mechanism: Imported components and technology licences; modest exports; +3% => ~-0.5.
Beta 1.7-1.8, 1y vol 38%, stock +57% in 12m at 50x P/E; CLSA 'cautious' / 43% downside from valuation (NDTV Profit 2026-10-15).
Small defence/naval systems revenue; sympathy with the DAC Rs2.12 lakh cr clearances.
